title: Passing Data by Pointer or Reference
learningObjectives: Explain passing data by pointer or reference.
Describe pointer/reference or lifetime rules involved.
Trace a simple memory access or ownership operation.
Recognize common undefined behavior and safety risks.
Choose a safer approach for a practical task.

understand.concept: Pointer parameters can express optional data or modify caller objects; reference parameters express required aliases. Value parameters copy objects.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing parameter style clarifies function contracts and copying costs.
understand.explain: Use const reference for read-only large objects; use reference for intentional mutation; pointer when nullable/indirection is meaningful.

examples.title: Optional pointer parameter
examples.explanation: Pointer parameter communicates that null may be supplied.

examples.title: Required reference
examples.explanation: Reference parameter requires a valid object and modifies it.

examples.title: Return value avoids alias
examples.explanation: A value return avoids a lifetime-sensitive reference.

examples.title: Choose parameter style
examples.explanation: Pointer version can represent absence; reference version requires an object.

practise.guidedTask: Trace the five Passing Data by Pointer or Reference examples. Mark each pointer/reference's target, object lifetime, mutability and whether dereferencing is valid.
practise.independentTask: Build a small C++ exercise showing passing data by pointer or reference. Include safe cases and deliberately describe (but do not execute) one invalid case. Demonstrate how ownership or lifetime is managed.
hints: Draw pointer arrows to live objects.
Use nullptr for empty pointers and check before dereferencing.
Keep pointer arithmetic within one array.
Distinguish pointer constness from pointee constness.
Prefer value returns, containers and smart pointers to manual ownership.

questions.explanation: Reference requires an object to bind to.
const reference avoids copies and mutation.
Returning by value avoids aliasing local storage.
